newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU health chief attacks tobacco industry. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU health chief attacks tobacco industry. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: European Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn renewed his attack on the tobacco industry Friday, condemning a cigarette price war as a ploy to lure new smokers in the face of publicity bans.

"This is a cynical attempt by the tobacco companies to recruit new smokers, which also reflects the increasing constraint on other marketing strategies," Flynn said in a statement to mark annual World No-Tobacco Day Saturday.

Flynn, the EU's top health official, said he was "very concerned about the strategy of some tobacco companies who have launched price reduction campaigns". (Corrects to make clear Flynn did not name specific companies).
A squeeze on advertising has seen cigarette firms increasingly resorting to price cuts, promotions, direct-marketing campaigns and prize draws to keep their brands in the public eye.
Flynn hailed plans by Britain's new Labour government for a national ban on tobacco ads and sponsorship of sports events.

Britain's announcement has raised Commission hopes of getting a total EU-wide ban on cigarette ads, after five years of resistance from a blocking minority of EU governments. Flynn is to put the issue to EU health ministers on June 5.
